title: Every good regulator of a system must be a model of that system
paper_title: The regulator is a model: does an AI system know the disturbances it claims to regulate?
paper_frame: Conant and Ashby proved that a regulator which is as simple as it can be and still regulates well must contain a model of the system it regulates. For an AI system that runs itself, the model is its register of failure modes, and each entry is only a model if something watches for it. We count.
data: Theory. The result is a theorem about regulators and the systems they regulate; the application to software is ours.
summary: A regulator that does its job well, with no unnecessary complexity, is a model of the thing it regulates: what it does mirrors the structure of what it faces. For an autonomous software system this means its list of failure modes is its model of the environment, and a failure mode that nothing detects is a part of the environment the regulator does not model.
limits: Reading. The source was not machine-read for this paper: its argument is stated in our own words from the publication's well-known content, with no quotation, and a reader should check the claim against the source linked above.
Reading of the theorem. The theorem is about the minimal regulator under stated conditions; we use it as a design test (every named disturbance has a detector), not as a proof about this system.
Declared versus observed. A detector that exists is not a detector that passes today; the share counts declared detectors.

misperception.belief: A capable enough AI system does not need an explicit model of what can go wrong; it will cope.
misperception.short: A capable AI needs no explicit model of its failures.
misperception.counter: A regulator that does its job well must contain a model of what it regulates. In software that model is a register of failure modes, each one watched by a detector, and it can be counted.

findings.claim: The register of failure modes is the system's model of its environment. A mode with no detector is a part of that environment the regulator does not model, so the system cannot respond to it. We count the share of registered modes that have at least one detector.

mechanisms.how: every failure mode is a row with trigger, symptom, blast radius, detection and root cause
each detector names the failure mode it watches
a mode nothing watches fails the audit

findings.concern: A model that is never checked against the world
findings.claim: A model of the environment goes stale unless something compares it with the environment. Every loop must declare a closing probe and a server-side owner, so the register of loops is also checked against what actually runs.

mechanisms.how: each loop has an expected interval, so a loop that stops is read from recorded beats
a manager with no loop is a title, not a regulator
